text.title: Business Model Research Failure Modes
text.summary: Antipatterns observed in real deployments of Business Model Research. Each ties a symptom to a root cause and a concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Model assumes 20-30% marketplace take rate. Assuming 20-30% take rate for a new marketplace.
antipattern.root-cause: Pattern-match to aspirational claims; LLM seeded by founder language. Real successful marketplaces compress to 5-15% as suppliers gain leverage (Etsy 6.5%, Airbnb 14%, Upwork 10%). Agents assume high take rates because they pattern-match aspirational claims.
antipattern.fix: Cap take-rate at 5-15% unless 10-K evidence supports higher; Etsy 6.5%, Airbnb 14%, Upwork 10% are the comparables.

antipattern.symptom: Cost Structure block reuses revenue numbers; LTV inflated. Using revenue as if it were profit in the Canvas Cost Structure block. Margin laziness: agent uses revenue as if it were profit; require a Cost Structure block before any LTV cell renders.
antipattern.root-cause: Author skipped gross-margin sourcing. Gross margin must be sourced separately; AI-heavy products run 30-50% due to inference costs, not 80% SaaS folklore. Missing the Cost Structure block makes LTV:CAC unreliable.
antipattern.fix: Source gross margin from a comparable 10-K or run an explicit COGS breakdown; AI-heavy SaaS often runs 30-50% margin, not 80%.

antipattern.symptom: Model claims 15% freemium conversion with no citation. Modeling freemium conversion at 15% without evidence.
antipattern.root-cause: Hallucinated benchmark from blog folklore. Floor conversion is 2% (consumer) / 5% (B2B). Claims above these require an empirical citation or a Soft tag.
antipattern.fix: Floor at 2% consumer / 5% B2B; require an empirical citation or Soft-tag the cell.

antipattern.symptom: Same monthly churn applied for 36 months. Static churn: one churn number for 36 months; require cohort-variable modeling (month-1 churn is 3-10x month-12).
antipattern.root-cause: Author used the simplest formula they remembered.
antipattern.fix: Model month-1 churn 3-10x month-12; cohort-variable churn before any LTV cell renders (rule cohort-variable-churn).

antipattern.symptom: Churn hallucination: model invents 2%/month "industry standard" — require a Baremetrics or ChartMogul benchmark URL or a 10-K citation.
antipattern.root-cause: The model fills the churn cell from training-data folklore instead of a sourced benchmark; nothing in the prompt demanded a URL.
antipattern.fix: Every churn cell is Hard-tagged with a Baremetrics / ChartMogul URL or a 10-K citation, or Soft-tagged and excluded from the P50 verdict.

antipattern.symptom: ARPU vs ARR confusion: monthly and annual numbers mixed in the same LTV calc — LTV is off by 12x and goes unnoticed.
antipattern.root-cause: Comparables publish annual figures while the formula expects monthly; the unit is never written next to the number.
antipattern.fix: State the period unit on every ARPU, churn and CAC cell; normalise to monthly before the LTV formula runs.

antipattern.symptom: Confirmation bias: founder mentions "$10M ARR by year 3" — agent reverse-engineers customer count and price; pre-commit Canvas before sharing the target.
antipattern.root-cause: A revenue target in the prompt anchors every downstream estimate; the agent solves for the target instead of for the evidence.
antipattern.fix: Withhold revenue targets until the Canvas and P10/P50/P90 bands are committed; compare to the target only in the verdict step.

antipattern.symptom: Output drift: each rerun rewrites the entire Canvas; lock headings to business-model-canvas.md and only fill cells; version the file.
antipattern.root-cause: Free-form regeneration has no anchor, so cell positions and wording move on every run and the assumptions ledger cannot be diffed.
antipattern.fix: Use `templates/business-model-canvas.md` headings verbatim, fill cells only, and bump the file version on every rerun.
